data.name: quick_friedman
data.problem: Learn the Friedman #1 nonlinear regression function from noisy samples.
objectives: Learn a regression model from simulated data (friedman) that solves: Learn the Friedman #1 nonlinear regression function from noisy samples.
Select methods by validation rmse only; the test split is used exactly once, at the end
Stay within 150 worker-seconds of compute and 350 s wall time
Eliminate weak approaches with cheap feasibility checks before spending substantial compute

data.title: ridge on 'raw' features
data.hypothesis: L2-regularised linear least squares; strong baseline for smooth near-linear inverse maps. Using 'raw' features tests whether a linear learner captures the target map under the classical statistical learning: linear, kernel and instance-based models with careful regularisation lens.

data.title: pls on 'log' features
data.hypothesis: Partial least squares; projects correlated features onto a few latent directions. Using 'log' features tests whether a linear learner captures the target map under the classical statistical learning: linear, kernel and instance-based models with careful regularisation lens.

data.title: extra_trees on 'raw' features
data.hypothesis: Extremely randomised trees; lower variance than random forests, fast. Using 'raw' features tests whether a ensemble learner captures the target map under the tree ensembles and gradient boosting for robust nonlinear function approximation lens.

data.title: random_forest on 'raw' features
data.hypothesis: Bagged decision trees; robust, little tuning, handles interactions. Using 'raw' features tests whether a ensemble learner captures the target map under the tree ensembles and gradient boosting for robust nonlinear function approximation lens.

data.title: torch_mlp on 'raw' features
data.hypothesis: PyTorch MLP (LayerNorm, GELU, AdamW, cosine LR, early stopping). Uses a GPU if allocated. Using 'raw' features tests whether a neural learner captures the target map under the neural networks: architecture, regularisation and optimisation choices lens.

data.title: mlp_sklearn on 'log' features
data.hypothesis: scikit-learn multilayer perceptron (Adam, early stopping). Using 'log' features tests whether a neural learner captures the target map under the neural networks: architecture, regularisation and optimisation choices lens.

data.title: ridge on 'raw' features
data.hypothesis: L2-regularised linear least squares; strong baseline for smooth near-linear inverse maps. Using 'raw' features tests whether a linear learner captures the target map under the domain/physics-informed feature engineering that exploits the structure of the simulator's observations, paired with suitable learners lens.

data.title: kernel_ridge on 'log' features
data.hypothesis: Kernel ridge regression with an RBF kernel; smooth nonlinear interpolant, O(n^2) memory. Bandwidth gamma = gamma_mult / (n_features * Var(X)) (sklearn 'scale' heuristic times a multiplier). Using 'log' features tests whether a kernel learner captures the target map under the domain/physics-informed feature engineering that exploits the structure of the simulator's observations, paired with suitable learners lens.
